newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan church calls for election tolerance.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan church calls for election tolerance.

text.p: Nicaragua's top Catholic leader on Sunday made a call for tolerance and peace heading in to this country's landmark October 20 presidential election.

"The joy of the campaign is fine, but the fact that one person hits another for having a different opinion is not. We must end the violence," conservative Cardinal Miguel Obando y Bravo told reporters.

The vote will be Nicaragua's first presidential election since its eight-year war between U.S.-backed Contra rebels and the Marxist Sandinista government ended in 1990 following the election victory of President Violeta Chamorro.
Despite threats by bands of re-armed former Contra and Sandinista soldiers in remote regions of northern Nicaragua, the campaign has been relatively violence-free.

The election, however, remained polarised between former President Daniel Ortega of the left-wing Sandinista Front and Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance, leading to a war of words between the candidates.
Obando y Bravo, one of Nicaragua's most powerful figures, has repeatedly warned the top candidates to cool down their language and stop blaming each other for Nicaragua's bloody past.
His recent call for tolerance came after various members of the Catholic Church said they received threatening messages warning of violence against them after the October 20 elections.
"I think these things are the work of a few fanatics and are not directly the work of the leadership of a particular party," Obando y Bravo said.
The Cardinal carefully avoided supporting one party in the election campaign, but the Catholic Church has had a history of run-ins with the Sandinista Front.
In January Nicaraguan police arrested a group of people linked to the Sandinista party in connection with a series of 23 minor bombings of Catholic churches across Nicaragua.
The lowest point of relations between the Sandinistas and the Catholic Church came in March 1983 when Sandinista activists booed Pope John Paul II during a visit to Nicaragua.
